newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Peters says NZ dollar can help c/a deficit recover.
newsitem.headline: Peters says NZ dollar can help c/a deficit recover.

text.p: New Zealand Treasurer Winston Peters said on Wednesday he thought the recent strength of the New Zealand dollar had an impact on the growth of the country's current account deficit, and he recognised that a sympathetic dollar level would help that deficit recover.

In an interview with Reuters Financial Television in Sydney, monitored in Wellington, Peters said, "I think you have to say (the dollar) has been a contributing factor, and the improvement in the deficit will depend upon the capacity of our exporters to take advantage of new momentum in the economy and a more export-sympathetic dollar."
Peters commented that in the light of the government's expectations on the economy and the dollar "we haven't got (that) long range worry" about a climb towards six percent.

In March, Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash said current account deficits of six percent of GDP were unsustainable, and adjustment would occur voluntarily, or by constraints provided by markets in the form of substantial capital outflows.
